Part 2&3 事件 EVENTS

Describe a time when you encouraged someone to do something that he/she didn't want to do

描述一次你鼓励别人做他/她不想做的事

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a time when you encouraged someone to do something that he/she didn't want to do

  • Who he or she is (他/她是谁)
  • What you encouraged him/her to do (你鼓励他/她做什么)
  • How he/she reacted (他/她反应如何)
  • And explain why you encouraged him/her to do it (并解释你为什么鼓励他/她做这件事)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a time when you encouraged someone to do something that he/she didn't want to do

I'd like to talk about a time when I encouraged a friend of mine to do something he wasn't really keen on. The person I'm talking about is one of my closest friends, and we've known each other since high school. What I encouraged him to do was to keep preparing for the graduate school entrance exam, which we call 考研 in China. He had been studying for it for a while, but at some point he lost motivation and started thinking about giving up. He told me he felt the pressure was too much, and he wasn't sure the exam was worth all the effort. When I heard that, I tried to encourage him. I reminded him that he'd already come a long way, and that giving up now would mean all those months of study were wasted. I also told him that even if he didn't get into his first-choice university, the knowledge he'd gained would still help him in the future. His reaction was a bit mixed, to be honest. He listened to what I said and seemed to agree, but I could tell he was only half-listening, and he didn't really change his attitude afterwards. The reason I encouraged him is that I genuinely believed he had the ability to succeed. He's a hardworking person, and I thought the exam would open more doors for his career. Even though my encouragement didn't fully work, I still think it was the right thing to do, because sometimes people just need to hear that someone believes in them.

讲的是鼓励一个高中就认识的好朋友坚持考研。鼓励什么：他备考考研一段时间后失去动力想放弃，说压力太大，不确定值不值得。我怎么鼓励：提醒他已经走了很长的路，现在放弃等于几个月的努力白费；还告诉他即使没考上第一志愿，学到的知识以后也有用。他的反应：听了似乎同意，但明显只是听听而已，之后态度没真正改变。为什么鼓励：我真心相信他有能力成功，他勤奋，而且考研能为职业打开更多门。虽然鼓励没完全奏效，我仍觉得做对了，因为有时候人只是需要听到有人相信他。

Q2How can leaders encourage their employees?

I think leaders can encourage employees mainly by recognising their efforts and giving them clear goals. When people feel their work is noticed and appreciated, they tend to be more motivated. Leaders can also encourage employees by offering opportunities for growth, like training or promotions, which gives them something to work towards. On top of that, a supportive atmosphere, where mistakes are treated as learning rather than punishment, makes people more willing to try their best.

领导鼓励员工主要靠认可努力和给出清晰目标。当人们感到工作被看见、被欣赏，就会更有动力；还可以通过提供成长机会，如培训或晋升，让人有奔头；另外支持性的氛围，把错误当学习而不是惩罚，会让人更愿意全力以赴。

Q3When should parents encourage their children?

Parents should encourage their children especially when they face challenges or setbacks. For example, when a child fails an exam or loses a competition, that's the moment they need support the most, because they might feel discouraged and doubt themselves. Parents should also encourage children when they try something new, even if they're not very good at it at first. I think the key is to encourage effort rather than only results, so children learn that trying matters.

父母尤其应该在孩子面对挑战或挫折时鼓励他们。比如孩子考试失利或比赛输了，那是最需要支持的时刻，因为他们可能灰心、怀疑自己；孩子尝试新事物时也该鼓励，即使一开始做得不好。关键是鼓励努力而不是只看结果，让孩子明白尝试本身很重要。

Q4What kind of encouragement should parents give?

I think the most effective encouragement is specific rather than general. Instead of just saying 'well done', parents can point out what exactly the child did well, like 'you worked really hard on this project'. This kind of feedback helps children understand their strengths. Parents should also encourage children to keep going when things get difficult, rather than praising only easy successes. I'd say encouragement that focuses on effort and improvement is more valuable than praise for natural talent.

最有效的鼓励是具体的而不是笼统的。与其只说'做得好'，父母可以指出孩子具体哪里做得好，比如'你在这个项目上真的很努力'，这种反馈帮孩子了解自己的长处。父母还应该在困难时鼓励孩子坚持，而不是只表扬轻松的成功。关注努力和进步的鼓励比夸天赋更有价值。

Q5Do you think some people are better than others at persuading?

Yes, I definitely think some people are naturally better at persuading others. Some people have strong communication skills, so they can explain their ideas clearly and make them sound convincing. Others are good at reading people's emotions, which helps them choose the right words at the right moment. That said, persuasion is also a skill that can be learned with practice. People who speak often, like teachers or salespeople, usually become better at it over time, so I'd say it's a mix of natural ability and experience.

是的，有些人天生更会说服别人。有人沟通能力强，能把想法讲清楚、讲得有说服力；有人擅长读懂别人情绪，能在对的时机说对的话。不过说服也是可以练出来的技能，经常说话的人，比如老师或销售，会越练越好。所以是天分加经验。

Q6Should children do everything their parents ask them to do?

No, I don't think children should do everything their parents ask, because parents aren't always right. Some requests might be unreasonable, or based on outdated ideas, and blindly following them could harm the child's own development. However, I also think children should respect their parents and consider their advice seriously, since parents usually have more life experience. So I'd say the ideal situation is a balance, where children listen to their parents but also learn to make their own decisions as they grow older.

不，孩子不该什么都听父母的，因为父母不一定总是对的。有些要求可能不合理，或基于过时的观念，盲目服从可能损害孩子自身发展。不过孩子也应该尊重父母、认真考虑他们的建议，因为父母通常经验更多。理想状态是平衡：听父母的，但随着长大也学会自己做决定。

Q7How can employers encourage their staff?

Employers can encourage their staff in several practical ways. Fair pay and reasonable working hours are the basics, because people can't stay motivated if they feel underpaid or overworked. Beyond that, recognising good work publicly, like praising an employee in a meeting, can boost morale a lot. Employers can also encourage staff by giving them more responsibility and trusting them with important tasks, which makes people feel valued. I think a combination of fair treatment and genuine recognition works best.

雇主可以用几种实际方式鼓励员工。公平的薪酬和合理的工作时间是基础，觉得工资低或过度劳累的人很难保持动力；公开认可好工作，比如在会议上表扬员工，能大大提升士气；还可以给员工更多责任、信任他们做重要任务，让人感到被重视。公平待遇加真诚认可的组合最有效。
